newsitem.title: GREECE: Biggest Greek labour group calls one-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Biggest Greek labour group calls one-day strike.

text.p: Greece's biggest labour grouping, GSEE, plans a one-day strike for next Thursday to press economic demands for tax reforms, it said in a statement.
The General Confederation of Greek Workers, GSEE, wants tax brackets index-linked to inflation and a tax-free limit on income to rise to two million drachmas from one million now.
GSEE has criticised the socialist government's new tax law, saying it left tax exemptions for the wealthy while abolishing breaks which had been given to wage earners.
"This direction is unjust and cannot be accepted by the trade union movement," the confederation said.
GSEE is an umbrella body of trade unions representing more than a million public and private employees.
It is the latest in a string of groups to set industrial action for this month. Seamen, farmers and civil servants among others have called for action to protest against the 1997 budget and tax bill.
The socialist government was rocked by strikes in November and December but most strike action was called off ahead of the Christmas holidays. -- Steve Weeks, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
